item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Glad the tapestry misdirection worked - I was unsure about that, since, obviously, we and she both know it was the tapestry was never anything but a tapestry. (Though, of course, not all misdirection needs to fool the reader.)

I see what you're saying regarding those details; I'll probably edit some of those a little ('I wasn't in there for very long and I felt fine after.' could probably use a reword, for example).

The use of, 'I think it had opinions.' seemed clunky to me and took me out of the immersion. This is due to the fact that I just don't want the explanation to be, 'it's a sentient ruby.' Hmm, I'll try to clarify. I don't want the ruby to be sentient on the order of magnitude of a consciousness capable of having opinions.

I also see what you're saying. The idea I had was that this was her opinion, based on spending way too much time thinking about this topic, and it might or might not be true.

The idea I had (which I'm not sure comes across or not, and not sure if it needs to) is that the ruby might have opinions - sort of. It's perhaps barely sentient, and certainly has some kind of drive of its own, but it's also affected by the thoughts/emotions/etc of the people who've come into contact with it. So maybe it has an opinion of its own, or maybe it's just absorbed the opinion of someone else. Or maybe human beings are just determined to anthropomorphize everything and think that this thing must have a personality (and it must be malevolent) because they just can't wrap their heads around it otherwise. Which is the opinion I imagine the interviewer taking, at least until the end where Janice unknowingly mentions the Foundation.

Of course, I've gone through several takes on this SCP since I've been trying to rewrite it, so I could just scrap that by tomorrow and edit again :P

Will also keep the editing advice in mind.

The use of, 'I think it had opinions.' seemed clunky to me and took me out of the immersion. This is due to the fact that I just don't want the explanation to be, 'it's a sentient ruby.' Hmm, I'll try to clarify. I don't want the ruby to be sentient on the order of magnitude of a consciousness capable of having opinions.

As for the whole TL;DR thing, it is long. It reads well, which makes up for that. Any editing for length should preserve the feel of the piece. Perhaps there are some personal aspects that can be taken out and still strike this balance. Overall, I would probably make only slight reductions here and there.

Just a newbie's opinion. Don't go just by me.
